extraction_text: 持国 describes the strengths and qualities of his army, including their training, equipment, and support from renowned warriors.

attributes.details: 持国 lists the army's advantages: well-trained soldiers, diverse weapon mastery, support from famous warriors like 德罗纳, 毗湿摩, 成铠, 慈悯, 难降, 胜车, 福授, 毗迦尔纳, 德罗纳之子 (马嘶), 妙力之子 (沙恭尼), and 波力迦.

extraction_text: 持国 compares his army to a vast, roaring sea, protected by many heroes, but laments its destruction in battle.

attributes.details: 持国 uses sea imagery to describe the army's might, noting its protection by warriors like 德罗纳 and 毗湿摩, yet acknowledges its defeat.

extraction_text: 持国 questions the reason for his army's defeat, considering it unprecedented and possibly due to divine intervention favoring the 般度族.

attributes.details: 持国 wonders if the defeat is fated or caused by gods (众天神) helping the 般度族, referencing an unseen battle scale.

extraction_text: 持国 recalls 维杜罗's wise advice that his son 难敌 ignored, suggesting 维杜罗 foresaw these events.

attributes.relationships: 持国 is father to 难敌; 维杜罗 is a wise figure whose counsel was disregarded by 难敌.

extraction_text: 持国 concludes that the events might be preordained by the creator (创造主), implying inevitability.

attributes.details: 持国 suggests fate or divine will as the cause, accepting no other outcome.

extraction_text: Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that the calamity is his own fault due to unrighteous actions, and that Dhritarashtra, unlike Duryodhana, understood this.
Sanjaya states that Dhritarashtra's faults led to the dice game and the war with the Pandavas, and he must now accept the consequences.
Bhima, after scattering the Kaurava army with arrows, attacks all of Duryodhana's brothers.

characters: Duryodhana's brothers (including Dushasana, Durmukha, Durjaya, Jalasandha, Saha, etc.)
relationships: Bhima (Pandava) vs. Duryodhana and his brothers (Kauravas)

extraction_text: Bhima, surrounded by his determined cousins, enters their ranks fearlessly, compared to Indra entering the ranks of the Danavas.

supernatural_elements: Simile comparing Bhima to Indra (king of gods) fighting Danavas (demons)

extraction_text: Bhima rains down terrible arrows while being surrounded by hundreds of thousands of chariot warriors, but he ignores the Kaurava princes and kills their soldiers instead.
Bhima, realizing the Kauravas are determined to kill him, decides to kill them all, abandons his chariot, and charges into the Kaurava army with his mace.
Shikhandi, grandson of Prishata, leaves Drona and swiftly attacks Shakuni, son of Subala.
Shikhandi cuts through the Kaurava army and finds Bhima's empty chariot, then asks Bhima's charioteer, Vishoka, where Bhima is.
Vishoka tells Shikhandi that Bhima ordered him to wait, then charged into the Kaurava army alone with his mace, saying he would quickly destroy those who wanted to kill him.
Meng Guang (猛光), grandson of King Shuidi (水滴王), heard the words of his charioteer Chu You (除忧) and responded in the middle of the battlefield.
Meng Guang declared his loyalty to Bhima (怖军), stating he would not abandon his friend and relative in battle.
Meng Guang charged into the Bharata (婆罗多族) army, following Bhima's path marked by elephants felled by Bhima's mace.
Meng Guang saw Bhima burning the enemy army and routing kings in battle like a gale wind breaking trees.
The enemy army surrounded Bhima from all sides, showering him with arrows.
Meng Guang saw Bhima, the best warrior, charging forward while the terrible army and world-famous heroes attacked Bhima from all sides.
Meng Guang approached the wounded Bhima, who was fighting on foot with his mace despite arrow wounds, to console him.
Meng Guang quickly removed arrows from Bhima, placed him on his own chariot, embraced him warmly, and comforted him while surrounded by enemies.
In the fierce battle, Duryodhana (your son) approached his brothers and ordered them to kill Meng Guang, who had joined Bhima, to prevent him from harming their army.
Hearing this, the sons of Dhritarashtra (持国之子们) became furious and charged forward with raised weapons, following their elder brother's command.
The heroes tightened their bows, with bowstring and chariot wheel sounds shaking the earth, and showered Meng Guang with arrows like clouds covering a mountain with rain.
Meng Guang, unafraid in battle, also killed them with sharp arrows.

Seeing Duryodhana's sons surging forward, the young Meng Guang became extremely angry and wanted to kill the heroes before him, striking them with the powerful 'Mihun' (迷魂) weapon like Indra (因陀罗) striking the Danavas (提迭).
The wisdom and courage of these human heroes were struck by the 'Mihun' weapon, leaving them confused and unconscious in battle.
Seeing Duryodhana's sons dazed and unconscious as if their time had come, all Kuru (俱卢族) warriors fled in all directions with elephants, horses, and chariots.

relationships: Army fleeing after leaders are incapacitated

extraction_text: Drona encountered King Drupada and shot three sharp arrows at him.

attributes.relationship: Teacher-student turned enemies (due to past enmity)

extraction_text: King Drupada was hit by Drona in battle and remembered their old enmity, then left the battlefield.
Drona defeated King Drupada and blew his conch, terrifying all the Somakas.
Drona heard that the sons of Dhritarashtra (the Kauravas) were rendered unconscious by the 'Mohanastra' (delusion weapon) in battle.
Drona wanted to rescue the princes and quickly left that part of the battlefield.
Drona saw Bhima and Shikhandin (son of Drupada) roaming the vast battlefield.
Drona saw the Kauravas unconscious, took out the 'Prajna' weapon (wisdom weapon), and neutralized the 'Mohanastra'.
The Kauravas regained consciousness and re-entered battle, attacking Bhima and Shikhandin.
Yudhishthira called his army and instructed them to follow the battle tracks of Bhima and Shikhandin.
Yudhishthira sent twelve warriors led by Abhimanyu (son of Subhadra) to investigate the situation because he felt uneasy.
The warriors including Kekayas, sons of Draupadi, and Satyaki, with Abhimanyu at the front, broke through the Kaurava chariot formation.
The great archers with Abhimanyu at the front charged forward, while the Kaurava army, fearful of Bhima and stunned by Shikhandin, was unable to resist.

attributes.psychological_state: Fear and confusion in Kaurava army

extraction_text: The great archers with golden banners charged forward to rescue Shikhandin and Bhima.
Seeing the great archers led by Abhimanyu, Shikhandin and Bhima were filled with joy and continued killing the Kaurava army.
Shikhandin suddenly saw his teacher Drona charging and stopped killing the Kauravas to focus on Drona.
Shikhandin placed Bhima on a Kekaya chariot and angrily charged at Drona.
Drona, enraged, quickly cut Shikhandin's bow with a crescent-headed arrow.
Remembering he ate his master's food, Drona shot hundreds of arrows at Shikhandin to repay Duryodhana.
Shikhandin took another bow and shot seventy gold-feathered arrows sharpened on stone at Drona.
Drona again cut his bow and quickly shot four sharp arrows at his four horses.
Drona killed the horses and then killed Shikhandin's charioteer with a crescent-headed arrow.
Shikhandin quickly jumped from his destroyed chariot and boarded Abhimanyu's great chariot.
Drona's army, along with chariots, elephants, and horses, trembled before Bhima and Shikhandin.
Drona, with his immense power, routed the army, and all the great warriors were unable to stop him.
Duryodhana regained consciousness and covered the unshakable Bhima with a shower of arrows.
Duryodhana's brothers, remembering their previous strategy to subdue the fearsome Bhima, resolved to subdue him again.
Bhima, in great anger, attacked Duryodhana's brothers, shooting arrows at Chitrasena and others.
Twelve great warriors led by Abhimanyu, following Yudhishthira's orders, pursued Duryodhana's brothers, causing them to abandon Bhima.

attributes.relationships: Abhimanyu leads warriors under Yudhishthira's command; Duryodhana's brothers retreat

extraction_text: Bhima continued to pursue Duryodhana's brothers, unwilling to let them escape alive.
Duryodhana and his warriors attacked Bhima, Shikhandin, and Abhimanyu together.
Abhimanyu killed Vikarna's horses and shot twenty-five small arrows at him, forcing Vikarna to abandon his chariot and board Chitrasena's.

attributes.relationships: Vikarna and Chitrasena are brothers; Abhimanyu attacks both

extraction_text: Dushasana (难胜) and Vikarna (毗迦尔纳) fired five iron arrows at Abhimanyu (迦尔希尼/激昂), who remained unmoved like Mount Meru.

attributes.supernatural_element: Abhimanyu's steadfastness compared to Mount Meru

extraction_text: Duryodhana (难降) fought against the five Kekaya brothers in battle.
The sons of Draupadi (德罗波蒂) angrily intercepted Duryodhana, each firing three arrows at him.

attributes.relationship: Draupadi's sons seeking revenge for their mother's humiliation by Duryodhana

extraction_text: Duryodhana, though wounded, retaliated by firing sharp arrows at Draupadi's sons.

attributes.description: Duryodhana bled brilliantly like mountain streams carrying minerals

extraction_text: Bhishma (毗湿摩) drove back the Pandava army in battle like a herdsman driving cattle.

attributes.relationship: Bhishma as Kaurava commander fighting against his grandsons, the Pandavas

extraction_text: Arjuna (普利塔之子/阿周那) sounded the Gandiva bow and slaughtered enemies on the right side of the army.
Fierce battle resulted in headless torsos, blood like ocean water, and warriors crossing the army ocean using chariots as boats.

attributes.description: Graphic depiction of war carnage with supernatural comparisons

extraction_text: As sunset approached, Duryodhana charged forward eager to kill Bhima in battle.

attributes.relationship: Longstanding enemies, with Bhima having vowed to kill Duryodhana

extraction_text: Bhima confronted Duryodhana, declaring his long-awaited moment to kill him and end the suffering of Kunti and Draupadi.

attributes.relationship: Bhima seeks revenge for Draupadi's humiliation and the Pandavas' exile

extraction_text: Bhima accused Duryodhana of being a gambler who insulted the Pandavas, following Karna and Shakuni's advice, and ignoring Krishna's pleas.

attributes.relationship: Bhima recounts Duryodhana's offenses against the Pandavas and Krishna

extraction_text: Bhima vowed to kill Duryodhana and his friends to avenge past crimes.
Bhima fired twenty-six fiery arrows at Duryodhana, hitting his bow, charioteer, horses, and canopy.

attributes.description: Bhima's powerful attack with arrows compared to thunderbolts

extraction_text: Bhima shot three arrows and cut off the shining, high-quality banner.
After cutting it, he roared in front of Duryodhana's son.
The auspicious banner studded with various gems suddenly fell from the chariot to the ground, like lightning separating from a cloud.
All the kings saw the beautiful, jewel-studded banner of King Duryodhana of the Kuru dynasty broken.
Then the great warrior Bhima, as if laughing, shot ten arrows at Duryodhana in battle, like attacking an elephant with a goad.
The best charioteer of the Sindhu clan, King Shalya, closely followed Duryodhana, taking on the important task of rear guard.
The immensely powerful Kuru descendant Duryodhana could not withstand the attack, and the best charioteer Kripa placed him on his chariot.
King Duryodhana, struck by Bhima's iron club in battle, sat on the chariot seat in pain.
Shalya wanted to kill Bhima, surrounded him with several chariots, and blocked his path.
The brave Abhimanyu, Yudhamanyu, the Kekaya brothers, and the sons of Draupadi fought with your sons.
Eight famous excellent princes and great archers surrounded Abhimanyu's chariot.
The noble-minded Abhimanyu quickly attacked, shooting five straight arrows at each of them; these arrows were like thunderbolts, like Death, shot from his wonderful bow.

attributes.supernatural_element: Arrows compared to thunderbolts and Death

extraction_text: They could not endure it and showered sharp arrows on the excellent charioteer Abhimanyu, like clouds raining on Mount Meru.
Abhimanyu, skilled in warfare, fought fiercely, and though attacked, he still shook your army, like Indra shaking the great Asuras in the battle between gods and Asuras.
Then this best charioteer, as if dancing on the battlefield, shot fourteen terrible crescent-shaped arrows like snakes, shattering Vikarna's banner, charioteer, and horses.
The mighty son of Subhadra shot other yellow arrows sharpened on stone at Vikarna.
These heron-feathered arrows struck Vikarna, pierced his body, and fell to the ground, shining like snakes.
Seeing Vikarna struck by arrows, his brothers rushed toward the warriors led by Abhimanyu.
Filled with anger, they fought fiercely, quickly approaching these warriors standing on chariots, shining like the sun, and killing each other.
Shrutakarma shot seven fast arrows at Shrutakirti, cut off his banner with one arrow, and shot seven arrows at his charioteer.
He rushed forward, killed six horses clad in golden armor, swift as the wind, with arrows, and struck down the charioteer.
The great warrior Shrutakirti, standing on a chariot with dead horses, filled with anger, threw a discus like a burning great comet.
This shining discus pierced the famous Shrutakarma's broad armor and went into the ground.
The mighty Satyaki saw Shrutakirti's chariot disabled and, in front of all the armies, placed him on his own chariot.
英雄闻称在战斗中冲向胜军，想要杀死他。
胜军用锋利的剃刀箭射断闻称挽开的弓。
百军看见同胞兄弟闻称的弓被射断，冲到那里，像狮子那样连声吼叫。
百军挽开硬弓，迅速向胜军发射四支箭。
百军又搭上一支能穿透一切铠甲的利箭，用力射击胜军的心窝。
丑耳就在兄弟胜军身边，愤怒至极，在战斗中射断百军的弓。

attributes.relationship: 丑耳与胜军是兄弟，与百军敌对

extraction_text: 百军取出另一张良弓，搭上锋利的箭，招呼丑耳并射出箭。
百军用一支箭射断丑耳的弓，用两支箭射击御者，又向丑耳射出七支箭。
百军用十二支锋利的箭全歼丑耳的黑斑马。
愤怒的百军用力发射一支月牙箭，击中丑耳的心窝。
看到丑耳受伤，五位大勇士从四面包围百军，想要杀死他。

characters: 五位大勇士（羯迦夜族五兄弟）
attributes.relationship: 羯迦夜族兄弟与百军敌对

extraction_text: 著名的百军被箭雨覆盖，羯迦夜族五兄弟满腔愤怒，冲了过去。
丑面、难胜、难耐、胜敌和御敌这些著名的勇士满腔愤怒，一起冲向羯迦夜族兄弟。

attributes.relationship: 般度族方与羯迦夜族敌对

extraction_text: 英雄们手持弓箭，铠甲和旗帜美丽，冲入敌方军队，犹如狮子从一座森林进入另一座森林。
战斗激烈，战车和大象碰撞，场面极其恐怖，互相残杀，互相施暴，扩充阎摩的王国。
太阳落山，战斗依然激烈，车兵和马兵成千成千倒下。
愤怒的福身王之子毗湿摩用笔直的箭歼灭般度族军队，用箭把般遮罗军队送往阎摩殿。

attributes.relationship: 毗湿摩（俱卢族方）与般度族方敌对

extraction_text: 大弓箭手毗湿摩击溃般度族军队，下令收兵，返回自己的营地。
法王坚战见到猛光和狼腹怖军，亲吻他俩的头，也高兴地返回营地。
